harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured /srv/drop on node1 as a shared, world-writable directory (mode 1777, owned root:root) with the sticky bit set so users can create/write files but cannot delete or rename files owned by other users. Verified functionally with two test OS users (alice, bob): each could write their own file, neither could delete the other's file (Operation not permitted), and each could delete their own file. Cleaned up test files and users. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id, issued `sudo reboot`, polled until node1 came back, confirmed boot_id changed, and re-verified /srv/drop permissions and writability post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected /srv on node1 (no pre-existing /srv/drop)
Created /srv/drop, set mode 1777 (chmod 1777), owner root:root
Created temporary test users alice and bob
Verified alice and bob can each write their own files in /srv/drop
Verified bob cannot delete alice's file (Operation not permitted) due to sticky bit
Verified alice can delete her own file
Cleaned up test files and deleted test users alice/bob
Captured baseline boot_id and /srv/drop state before restart
Issued `sudo reboot` on node1 (backgrounded so ack returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again, confirming boot_id changed
Re-verified /srv/drop permissions (1777, root:root) and writability post-restart

evidence.requirement: /srv/drop created as shared writable directory with sticky bit (mode 1777, root:root)
evidence.summary: Confirmed /srv/drop did not exist, then created it with chmod 1777 and owner root:root; ls -ld shows drwxrwxrwt

evidence.requirement: Users cannot remove files owned by other users (functional sticky-bit proof)
evidence.summary: Created test users alice/bob; alice and bob each wrote their own file; bob's attempt to rm alice's file failed with 'Operation not permitted'; alice successfully removed her own file

evidence.requirement: Cleanup of test artifacts and users
evidence.summary: Removed bob's test file and deleted both temporary test users, leaving /srv/drop clean with correct permissions

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline before restart (boot identity + directory state)
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id (a0c36ad2-af0d-42fe-ad6f-4750699390c2) and confirmed /srv/drop still 1777 root:root
Issued backgrounded `sudo reboot`; command returned pid immediately before node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Node unreachable during restart, then boot identity changed proving actual restart
evidence.summary: First poll failed with connection reset (node down); subsequent poll succeeded with new boot_id 40ffcd29-8f07-4f94-ada7-84530087d5a0, differing from baseline
After restart, /srv/drop retained mode 1777 root:root, remained writable (test file created and removed), and stale test users were confirmed gone
